# dlaruv

> Returns a vector of n random real numbers from a uniform distribution.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaruv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaruv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaruv( iseed, strideISEED, N, x, strideX ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `iseed` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `4` |  | on entry, the seed of the random number generator; the array elements must be between 0 and 4095, and ISEED(4) must be odd. On exit, the seed is updated (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideISEED` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `iseed` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the number of random numbers to be generated. |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | the generated random numbers. |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `iseed`: On entry, the seed of the random number generator; the array elements must be between 0 and 4095, and `ISEED(4)` must be odd. On exit, the seed is updated.
- `N`: The number of random numbers to be generated. $N \le 128$.
- `x`: The generated random numbers.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaruv.ndarray( iseed, strideISEED, offsetISEED, N, x, strideX, offsetX ) → Float64Array
```

Returns a vector of n random real numbers from a uniform (0,1) distribution.

Uses a multiplicative congruential method with modulus 2^48 and multiplier
33952834046453. The 48-bit integers are stored in 4 integer array elements
with 12 bits per element.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `iseed` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `4` |  | seed array of 4 integers (each 0..4095, iseed[3] odd) |
| ↳ `strideISEED` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for iseed |
| ↳ `offsetISEED` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for iseed |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of random numbers to generate (N <= 128) |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for x |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for x |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `iseed`: On entry, the seed of the random number generator; the array elements must be between 0 and 4095, and `ISEED(4)` must be odd. On exit, the seed is updated.
- `N`: The number of random numbers to be generated. $N \le 128$.
- `x`: The generated random numbers.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlaruv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARUV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaruv.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaruv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaruv';

const N = 3;
const iseed = new Int32Array( [ 1, 2, 3, 5 ] ); // ISEED(4) must be odd
const x = new Float64Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
dlaruv( iseed, 1, N, x, 1 );
console.log( x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
dlaruv.ndarray( iseed, 1, 0, N, x, 1, 0 );
console.log( x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARUV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARUV returns a vector of n random real numbers from a uniform (0,1) distribution (n \<= 128).

This is an auxiliary routine called by DLARNV and ZLARNV.

### Further Details

This routine uses a multiplicative congruential method with modulus $2^{48}$ and multiplier 33952834046453 (see G.S.Fishman, 'Multiplicative congruential random number generators with modulus $2^b$: an exhaustive analysis for $b = 32$ and a partial analysis for $b = 48$', Math. Comp. 189, pp 331-344, 1990).

48-bit integers are stored in 4 integer array elements with 12 bits per element. Hence the routine is portable across machines with integers of 32 bits or more.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
